_comment: Free-text questions of the kind a tradesperson types, with bindings the query text itself rules out. scripts/measure-query-fill.mjs builds its corpus from each tile's worked example, so every number in it is labelled, in field order, with no distractors -- which is why it reports zero wrong values while these reproduce. Each row asserts what a number must NOT become, because that is what the query text settles on its own; which tile ought to answer is a separate question this fixture deliberately does not take a position on.
_schema: rows[]: { query, tile, mustNotBind: { field: value }, why }
_experiment_not_taken: Dropping the same-family unit conversion in the unit-agreement phase (fill only on an EXACT unit match) takes the wrong bindings below from 2 to 1 and leaves measure-query-fill.mjs completely unchanged: 4,349 / 7,184 fields, 0 wrong. That reads as free, and it is not. The recovery corpus is built from worked examples, so every number in it carries the field's OWN unit and no same-family conversion is ever exercised -- the harness cannot see what removing it would cost, which is a reader writing 3 ft into a field measured in inches. Refusing that is a real capability loss neither harness measures. Recorded so the next attempt does not spend the experiment again, and does not mistake an unmeasured cost for no cost.

rows.query: wire size for a 50 amp circuit 90 feet away
rows.why: 90 is the run length in feet. Binding it to the conductor's insulation temperature rating is wrong and plausible: 90 C is a real rating, so an agent has nothing to notice.

rows.query: fall protection anchor for a 310 lb worker and 6 ft free fall
rows.why: 6 is the free-fall distance in feet. Bound to a headcount it sizes an anchorage for six workers.

rows.query: control joints for a 20x30 slab 4 inches thick
rows.why: 20 is a plan dimension with no unit; the thickness is written with one, four inches, in the same sentence.

rows.query: how many studs for a 40 ft wall 16 on center
rows.why: 480 inches is the 40 ft wall length converted into a stud-depth field. Feet and inches share a dimension; a wall and a stud do not share a meaning.

rows.query: how many 4x8 sheets for a 24 by 40 floor
rows.why: Eight inches converted to feet, into a field for the length of a sheet. No sheet is 0.67 ft long.

rows.query: fence posts for 100 ft of fence 8 ft apart
rows.why: "100 ft of fence" is the fence; "8 ft apart" is the post spacing. Reading each name forward onto the NEXT number swapped them (2026-11-16).

rows.query: lumber for a 12 ft wall 8 ft tall 16 on center
rows.why: The wall is 12 ft long and 8 ft tall. "wall" read forward gave the length 8 ft, and the 8 ft height, which this tile has no field for, must not become a 96 in stud spacing.

rows.query: gallons in a 10 ft round pool 4 ft deep
rows.why: 10 ft is the pool's diameter; "4 ft deep" is its depth. The diameter, converted to 120 in, filled the depth.

rows.query: how many tiles for a 10 by 12 floor 12 inch tile
rows.why: A floor-tile count ranked the shower pan first, and the 12 inch TILE filled the mortar bed's thickness at the drain. It now reaches tile-count.

rows.query: how many studs for a 40 ft wall with 2 corners and 2 openings
rows.why: The 40 ft wall, converted to 480 in, was the only evidence for the siding tile and became its siding exposure.

rows.query: fence 200 ft with 2 gates
rows.why: 200 ft of fence, converted to 2,400 in, became a tree's trunk diameter on a calculator the question never asked for.

rows.query: concrete block count 40 ft wall 8 ft tall
rows.why: The 40 ft wall, converted to inches, filled the mortar joint thickness.

rows.query: how much weight can a 2x10 span 12 ft
rows.why: The 12 ft span, converted to 144 in, filled the joist's tributary width.

rows.query: how many lumens for a 12 by 12 room
rows.why: One side of the room became the lumens each luminaire puts out.

rows.query: solar panels for 900 kwh per month
rows.why: 900 kWh per month is a usage rate, not a 900 kWh battery.

rows.query: subcooling 300 psig liquid 95 f r410a
rows.why: 95 F is the liquid-line temperature; with no temperature word in the query the bare f was dropped and the 95 became a vertical lift in feet.

rows.query: gas meter clock 1 cubic foot dial 30 seconds
rows.why: 30 seconds per revolution, read forward from "dial", became a 30 cubic foot test dial.

rows.query: horsepower from torque 400 ft-lb at 5000 rpm
rows.why: The question hands over the torque and asks for horsepower; the word torque chose Solve for torque, and the tile refused for want of a horsepower.

rows.query: how many bags of quikrete for a 4x4 slab 4 inches
rows.why: A 4x4 slab is four feet by four; the lumber rewrite made it a 4 in wide stick and the slab 0.33 ft wide.

rows.query: slope percent 2 ft rise over 50 ft
rows.why: The 2 ft is the rise and the 50 ft the run; they came back as a 2 ft run and a 600 in fall.

rows.query: 2x4 studs 16 on center
rows.why: The 2 is the stick's nominal size, written by the lumber rewrite as 2 in, and its unit alone put it in the stud spacing.

rows.query: joist span 2x10 16 inch
rows.why: The 2 of 2x10, as 2 in, became a 0.17 ft joist span because "span" sat in front of it.

rows.query: board feet in 2x6 8 ft long 20 pieces
rows.why: A 2x6 is 2 thick by 6 wide; the lumber rewrite's 'width' put the 2 in Width and the 6 went nowhere.

rows.query: tankless water heater 5 gpm 70 degree rise
rows.why: A 70 degree rise is a temperature difference; it filled the target outlet temperature by unit alone.

rows.query: retaining wall blocks 50 ft long 3 ft tall
rows.why: '50 ft long' named only the block face length, because the wall's own label said 'Wall run'; the 50 ft became a 600 in block.

rows.query: cutting speed 300 sfm 2 inch diameter
rows.why: The diameter label's unit sat behind a colon ('in: cutter for mill/drill'), so the chip load was the only inch field and took the 2 inch diameter.

rows.query: tire size 265/70r17 diameter
rows.why: A P-metric tire size read as the fraction 265/70; '70r' has no word boundary, so the fraction veto missed it.

rows.query: ladder angle 20 ft ladder 5 ft from wall
rows.why: '5 ft from wall' is the base offset, which this tile does not take; 'ladder' before it made it the ladder length, and the 20 ft ladder became the working height.

rows.query: ceiling height 8 ft room 12 by 12 cfm for 6 air changes
rows.why: 'room 12 by 12' was not seen as a plan (the surface word came first), so 'room 12' read as a 12 cu ft room volume and the tile answered 1.2 CFM.

rows.query: duct velocity 800 cfm 12 inch round
rows.why: The friction label '(in w.c. / 100 ft)' was read as inches by the leading-unit-word rule, so a 12 inch duct became a friction rate of 12.

rows.query: string size 400 w panels 600 v inverter voc 49
rows.why: The term floor reduced 'Inverter Vdc max' to the word 'inverter', so the exact-label tie-break handed it the module Voc of 49.

rows.query: 11 hour driving limit hours of service
rows.why: The 11 hours are driving time, which the tile has no field for; the unit alone put them in the weekly on-duty hours already used.

rows.query: crown molding for 12 by 14 room
rows.why: The room's 12 by 14 went to 'Trim stock length' and 'Total door-opening width' as if they were the plan's length and width; the room's perimeter is 52 ft.

rows.query: fertilizer for 10 acres 150 lb nitrogen 46-0-0
rows.why: 150 lb of nitrogen became the bag weight, the only field in pounds.
